This guide walks through understanding instant navigations, writing a route that navigates instantly, visualizing what's in the initial UI, and locking the behavior in with end-to-end tests.

## What "instant" means

A navigation is **instant** when the browser can start rendering the new page the moment the user clicks, with static, cached, and fallback content showing up right away, while the server streams the remaining content into its fallbacks.

00052| > **Good to know**: In an existing app, review the UI delivered by [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) before enabling Partial Prefetching. These links use the legacy full prefetch, and enabling Partial Prefetching changes their behavior.
00053| 
00054| Enable [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) in `next.config.ts`:
00055| 
00056| ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5}
00057| import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
00058| 
00059| const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
00060|   cacheComponents: true,
00061|   partialPrefetching: true,
00062| }
00063| 
00064| export default nextConfig
00065| ```
00066| 
00067| After enabling the flag, links using the default behavior, `prefetch="auto"`, or `prefetch={true}` prefetch the destination's App Shell. A link with `prefetch={true}` can also resolve cached URL-specific content, but it no longer includes uncached dynamic content from the legacy full prefetch. New projects can enable the flag without this audit because they have no legacy full prefetches to migrate.
00068| 
00069| > **Good to know**: When `cacheComponents` is enabled without a `partialPrefetching` value, Next.js logs a warning asking you to set it to `true` or `false`. Set `false` only to keep the previous prefetch behavior while you work through this guide. Both features will be enabled everywhere in the next major release, and the options will be removed.
00070| 
00071| ## What changes for `<Link>`
00072| 
00073| | `<Link>` prop                       | Before (Cache Components default)                              | After Partial Prefetching                                                                                                                              |
00074| | ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
00075| | `<Link href="/x">`                  | Prefetched the cached page render.                             | Prefetches the shared App Shell for `/x`.                                                                                                              |
00076| | `<Link href="/x" prefetch>`         | Prefetched the cached page render **and** any dynamic content. | Prefetches the App Shell, plus cached URL-specific content through [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) when `/x` reads it. |
00077| | `<Link href="/x" prefetch={false}>` | Disabled prefetching for this link.                            | Unchanged. Still disabled.                                                                                                                             |
00078| 
00079| The App Shell is shared across every link to a given route, regardless of dynamic params, so rendering many `<Link>`s to the same destination doesn't multiply the work.
00080| 
00081| ## Migrate existing full prefetches
00082| 
00083| Before Partial Prefetching, a `<Link>` whose effective `prefetch` value is `true` prefetches the complete destination, including uncached dynamic content. This includes `prefetch={true}`, the bare `prefetch` prop, and wrapper or conditional props that resolve to `true`. The default value, `prefetch="auto"`, and `prefetch={false}` don't use the legacy full prefetch.
00084| 
00085| A legacy full prefetch can include more UI than the navigation needs. In most cases, the primary content at the top of the destination should be available before navigation, while secondary or frequently changing content can stream afterward.
00086| 
00087| > **Good to know**: `cookies()` and `headers()` don't tie a prefetch to a URL. They vary per session, not per link, so the App Shell still carries session content. Only `params` and `searchParams` are [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data), which varies per link and can't be included in the shared App Shell.

00267| ### URL data
00268| 
00269| [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data) (`params`, `searchParams`) varies per link, so content that depends on it can't be included in the shared App Shell and streams in after navigation from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary. The links keep `prefetch={true}`, and [Prefetching URL data](#prefetching-url-data) covers prefetching the content ahead of the click.

00271| ### Real-time content
00272| 
00273| A prefetch of real-time content would be stale by the click, so there is nothing to preserve. Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary.
00274| 
00275| | Destination                                                                       | Recommendation                                                            |
00276| | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
00277| | [Fully static, or content already cached](#static-or-cached-content)              | Remove the now-redundant `prefetch={true}`.                               |
00278| | [Delivered uncached content you want kept ahead of the click](#uncached-content)  | Cache it with `use cache`, then remove `prefetch={true}`.                 |
00279| | [Delivered content that depends on `cookies()` or `headers()`](#session-content)  | Cache the lookup behind the session value, then remove `prefetch={true}`. |
00280| | [Reads URL data, or has cached content that depends on it](#url-data)             | Keep `prefetch={true}` to resolve the content ahead of the click.         |
00281| | [Delivers real-time content that must stay fresh per request](#real-time-content) | Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in.                   |

[Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prefetching) changes what a `<Link>` downloads for a Cache Components route. With Partial Prefetching enabled, a `<Link>` prefetches the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell): its static content and the cached content that doesn't depend on the URL. Next.js builds one App Shell per route and reuses it for every link to that route, rather than prefetching each link separately as it did before.

To prefetch more than the App Shell, a link can opt into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch can then resolve cached URL-specific content that depends on `params`, `searchParams`, or the full URL.

Along the way, Next.js surfaces [instant navigation](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) insights in development, naming the link or route to change.

[Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) can prerender a static shell while request-time content streams in. The shell can keep the route's layout, navigation, headings, and focused loading states visible instead of replacing the page with one broad fallback.

Apps written before Cache Components often await request data near the top of a layout or page. With Cache Components enabled, those routes may already have a small static shell, sometimes made up of one broad loading state.

In this guide, you'll learn how to expand the shell by tracing each data read to the UI that needs it, caching reusable work, and moving request-time work behind focused `<Suspense>` boundaries. These patterns keep important content available early and reserve space as the rest of the page streams in.

00093|

00095| 
00096| - Crashes, hangs, OOMs, or unexpected slowness
00097| - Incorrect behavior, output, errors, or diagnostics
00098| - Missing, unclear, or conflicting documentation
00099| - Unexpected CLI, codemod, Skill, or upgrade behavior and non-obvious workarounds
00100| 
00101| Continue the current user request without reporting immediately. Routine debugging is not feedback. Verify changes before retaining them as feedback candidates. Never retain code, logs, paths, URLs, secrets, personal information, or project-specific data.

00113| 
00114| ## Agent-guided upgrades
00115| 
00116| `next upgrade --agent` checks for an available upgrade, gathers the version-matched migration guides, and hands the task to a coding agent. The agent applies the changes and verifies the app:
00117| 
00118| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00119| npx next@canary upgrade --agent=latest
00120| ```
00121| 
00122| The experimental [`agentUpgrade`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/agentUpgrade) option shows security upgrade reminders during `next dev` and `next build` by default. 00123| 
00124| <span id="step-2-give-agents-runtime-visibility" />
00125| 
00126| ## Runtime visibility
00127| 
00128| Agents need both framework and browser state to verify a running application. Next.js and its supporting tools expose these complementary views as structured text.
00129| 
00130| First, `next dev` forwards browser console errors and warnings to the terminal (the [`logging.browserToTerminal`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/logging) config), so the output agents already read carries the client-side failures they're asked to fix.
00131| 
00132| `next dev` also writes its PID, port, and URL to `.next/dev/lock`. If you run `next dev` while another development server is already running for the project, the command prints the existing server's URL and PID, along with a command to stop it. Continue with the existing server when possible to avoid interrupting the active development session.
00133| 
00134| The **framework's view** comes from the [Next.js MCP server](/docs/app/guides/mcp) at `/_next/mcp`, which exposes the running dev server's routes, server logs, and compilation issues. Its `get_compilation_issues` and `compile_route` tools report whether the code compiles straight from the dev server, so an agent doesn't have to run a full `next build` to find out.
00135| 
00136| The [`next-dev-loop` skill](#next-dev-loop) adds the **browser's view** through [`agent-browser`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-browser), a CLI that exposes the DOM, console, network, and Web Vitals as structured text. The Skill opens `agent-browser` with React DevTools enabled, which also exposes the component tree and pending Suspense boundaries. An agent can run a command such as `react tree` and use the structured output to decide what to inspect next.
00137| 
00138| Together with the Next.js MCP server, `next-dev-loop` combines the framework's and the browser's perspectives into one edit-and-verify loop.
00139| 
00140| <span id="step-3-let-errors-drive-the-fixes" />
00141| 
00142| ## Built-in guidance for errors
00143| 
00144| With [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) enabled, a blocking error presents labeled fixes, each making a different trade-off. The dev overlay adds a **Copy prompt** button that packages the chosen fix into a paste-ready prompt. The prompt walks the agent through reading the matching error page, applying the canonical pattern, and verifying the result at runtime.
00145| 
00146| The same menu prints in the `next dev` terminal and in `next build` output, so an agent reading CI logs sees it too:
00147| 
00148| ```txt filename="Terminal"
00149| Route "/products/[slug]": Next.js encountered uncached data during prerendering.
00150| 
00151| `fetch(...)` or `connection()` accessed outside of `<Suspense>` prevents the route
00152| from being prerendered, blocking the page load and leading to a slower user experience.
00153| 
00154| Ways to fix this:
00155|   - [stream] Provide a placeholder with `<Suspense fallback={...}>` around the data access
00156|   - [cache] Cache the data access with `"use cache"` (does not apply to `connection()`)
00157|   - [block] Set `export const instant = false` to allow a blocking route
00158| 
00159| Learn more: https://nextjs.org/docs/messages/blocking-prerender-dynamic
00160|     at ProductPage (app/products/[slug]/page.tsx:52:32)
00161|     ...
00162| ```
00163| 
00164| `next dev` shows all validation errors with source-mapped stacks in the overlay and terminal. Production builds minify server code and stop after a route fails. Use [`next build --debug-prerender`](/docs/app/guides/building#debug-prerender-errors) to enable server source maps and continue checking other routes.
00165| 
00166| The `Learn more` link resolves to a per-error page under [`/docs/messages`](https://nextjs.org/docs/messages/blocking-prerender-dynamic) written for agents to read. Each page follows the same shape, with the canonical patterns for every fix, the trade-offs against the other fixes, and the gotchas an agent is likely to miss on a first attempt. The [Instant navigation guide](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation#ai-workflow) walks through the full loop an agent runs on these errors, from reading the insight to writing an `instant()` test that fails before the fix and passes once it's in place.
00167| 
00168| <span id="step-4-hand-multi-step-workflows-to-skills" />
00169| 
00170| ## Skills for multi-step workflows
00171| 
00172| Framework knowledge comes from the bundled docs, not from Skills. [Benchmark results](https://nextjs.org/evals) show that always-available context outperforms on-demand retrieval. Skills cover the tasks that are workflows rather than lookups, such as adopting Cache Components or Partial Prefetching across an app. Next.js Skills package these as structured instructions an agent installs and follows, sequencing the work and pointing at the relevant docs and [runtime tooling](#runtime-visibility) along the way.
00173| 
00174| You can [browse the source for these Skills](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/skills) in the Next.js repository and [find them on skills.sh](https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js).
00175| 
00176| The Skills serve three different workflow types:
00177| 
00178| - **Runtime foundations** such as `next-dev-loop` give any coding task a repeatable inspect, edit, and verify cycle.
00179| - **Interactive workflows** make broader changes with user checkpoints, such as adopting Cache Components or Partial Prefetching across an app.
00180| - **Unattended loops** work toward a verifiable goal and stop only for genuine decisions.
00181| 
00182| ### `next-dev-loop`
00183| 
00184| The [`next-dev-loop`](https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-dev-loop) runtime foundation verifies changes against a running dev server using the [MCP server](/docs/app/guides/mcp) and browser.
00185| 
00186| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00187| npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-dev-loop
00188| ```
00189| 
00190| Then give the agent this prompt:
00191| 
00192| ```prompt
00193| After every edit, verify the page still works at runtime using the next-dev-loop Skill.
00194| ```
00195| 
00196| ### `next-bundle-optimizer`
00197| 
00198| The [`next-bundle-optimizer`](https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-bundle-optimizer) skill uses Turbopack's bundle analyzer to identify sources of large client-side bundles that impact your site's initial load performance.
00199| 
00200| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00201| npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-bundle-optimizer
00202| ```
00203| 
00204| In audit-only mode, it produces a report without making any changes:
00205| 
00206| ```prompt
00207| Use the next-bundle-optimizer skill to produce a report of the initial load performance of this site.
00208| ```
00209| 
00210| You can also tell your agent to fix any issues, and it will optimize your site based on its findings. Or have it focus on a specific route by providing the route in the prompt.
00211| 
00212| ### `next-cache-components-adoption`
00213| 
00214| The [`next-cache-components-adoption`](https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-cache-components-adoption) Skill migrates an app to [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching):
00215| 
00216| 1. Turns the flag on and finds the routes that can't prerender.
00217| 2. Fixes them one feature at a time, checking in with you before moving on.
00218| 3. Confirms a feature against `next dev` and `next build` before leaving it.
00219| 
00220| The Skill supports both a series of pull requests and a single-branch migration.
00221| 
00222| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00223| npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-cache-components-adoption
00224| ```
00225| 
00226| Then give the agent this prompt:
00227| 
00228| ```prompt
00229| Adopt Cache Components in this project using the next-cache-components-adoption Skill.
00230| ```
00231| 
00232| ### `next-cache-components-optimizer`
00233| 
00234| The [`next-cache-components-optimizer`](https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-cache-components-optimizer) Skill expands a target route's static shell to include the useful UI you want available on an initial load:
00235| 
00236| 1. Writes a failing [`instant()`](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation#prevent-regressions-with-e2e-tests) test for the static-shell UI you named.
00237| 2. Refactors the route until it passes, often by moving a data read below a `<Suspense>` boundary.
00238| 3. Commits the passing test with the refactoring, so it catches future regressions.
00239| 
00240| Use it after adopting [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) to optimize an initial load or client navigation. To prefetch URL-specific content for an already-instant destination, use the [`next-partial-prefetching-optimizer`](#next-partial-prefetching-optimizer) instead.
00241| 
00242| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00243| npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-cache-components-optimizer
00244| ```
00245| 
00246| Then give the agent a prompt like:
00247| 
00248| ```prompt
00249| Optimize the static shell for /dashboard using the next-cache-components-optimizer Skill. On an initial load, the header and project list should be available immediately.
00250| ```
00251| 
00252| ### `next-partial-prefetching-adoption`
00253| 
00254| The [`next-partial-prefetching-adoption`](https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-partial-prefetching-adoption) Skill moves an app onto [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching), where links share one App Shell:
00255| 
00256| 1. Audits existing `<Link prefetch={true}>` navigations and identifies the prefetched UI to preserve.
00257| 2. Captures that UI in passing [`instant()`](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation#prevent-regressions-with-e2e-tests) tests before enabling Partial Prefetching, then migrates each destination until the same tests pass unchanged.
00258| 3. Enables the flag, resolves the URL-data insights it surfaces, and marks optional per-link prefetching candidates for later.
00259| 
00260| It needs [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) already adopted and a production-like build it can run for prefetch verification.
00261| 
00262| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00263| npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-partial-prefetching-adoption
00264| ```
00265| 
00266| Then give the agent this prompt:
00267| 
00268| ```prompt
00269| Adopt Partial Prefetching in this project using the next-partial-prefetching-adoption Skill.
00270| ```
00271| 
00272| ### `next-partial-prefetching-optimizer`
00273| 
00274| The [`next-partial-prefetching-optimizer`](https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-partial-prefetching-optimizer) Skill takes a target navigation or set of navigations and works toward the UI you want ready before each click:
00275| 
00276| 1. Turns the requested behavior for each navigation into a contract for what is prefetched, what waits for navigation, and when prefetching begins.
00277| 2. Captures each contract in an [`instant()`](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation#prevent-regressions-with-e2e-tests) test.
00278| 3. Applies the [Optimizing prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) patterns and keeps the passing tests as regression coverage.
00279| 
00280| It needs Cache Components and Partial Prefetching already adopted.
00281| 
00282| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00283| npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-partial-prefetching-optimizer
00284| ```
00285| 
00286| Then give the agent a prompt like:
00287| 
00288| ```prompt
00289| Make the product title instant when navigating from /products to /products/[id]. Use the next-partial-prefetching-optimizer Skill.
00290| ```
00291|

AI coding agents may rely on training data that predates the Next.js version installed in a project. To help agents use current APIs and verify their work, Next.js provides and evaluates version-matched documentation, managed project instructions, agent-guided upgrades, runtime tools, structured errors, reusable Skills, and optional agent feedback. See the results in the [Next.js agent evaluations](https://nextjs.org/evals).

For more background, read about the AI tooling introduced in [Next.js 16.2](/blog/next-16-2-ai) and [Next.js 16.3](/blog/next-16-3-ai-improvements).

## What is streaming?

In traditional server-side rendering, the server produces the full HTML document before sending anything. A single slow database query or API call can block the entire page. Streaming changes this by using [chunked transfer encoding](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Transfer-Encoding) to send parts of the response as they become ready. The browser starts rendering HTML while the server is still generating the rest.

This is especially impactful for pages that combine fast static content (headers, navigation, layout) with slower dynamic content (personalized data, analytics, recommendations). The static parts can be prerendered and served from a CDN, painting instantly, while the dynamic parts stream in from the server as they become ready.
